 Marcos hails 'impactful' PH chairship of ASEAN, cites over 100 outcomes
 by 
 Ruth Abbey Carlos
 Nov 17, 2026
 8:45 PM GMT+8
 President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. holds a press conference at the International Media Center at World Trade Center Metro Manila in Pasay City on Tuesday (Nov. 17, 2026) following the conclusion of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit and Related Summits. (PNA photo by Joan Bondoc) 
 MANILA – President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Tuesday described the Philippines’ 2026 chairship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) as “successful” and “impactful,” citing more than 100 outcome documents aimed at advancing regional cooperation and addressing shared challenges.
 Speaking to reporters at the International Media Center at World Trade Center Metro Manila in Pasay City, Marcos said the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits produced productive and candid discussions among member-states.
 “Over the past three days, we have been very productive, very candid, yet focused, resulting in impactful decisions that address the critical issues of the day. Across three pillars of ASEAN, the leaders acted on over 100 outcome documents,” he said.
 “These are not merely documents. These are frameworks, guidelines, and perspectives in advancing practical cooperation on key regional priorities.”
 He cited several key accomplishments under the Philippines’ 2026 ASEAN chairship, including progress in maritime cooperation, digital economy integration, energy connectivity, disaster response and child protection.
 Among the significant developments was the adoption of the concept note and terms of reference for the ASEAN Maritime Center, which will serve as a regional knowledge hub and provide advisory support on maritime-related initiatives and concerns.
 Marcos said the center is expected to promote evidence-based policymaking and facilitate the implementation of maritime priorities identified by ASEAN member-states.
 He also cited the adoption of the ASEAN Leaders' Declaration on Preventing Online Sexual Abuse and Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials in the Digital and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Enabled Environment.
 The declaration reinforces ASEAN's commitment to safeguarding children's rights and ensuring a safer digital environment amid the growing use of technology and AI, he said.
 Marcos also cited the unveiling of the updated ASEAN flag and emblem during Sunday's opening ceremony, reflecting Timor-Leste's accession as the regional bloc's 11th member.
 He likewise noted the expansion of the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia, with new signatories bringing the total number of high contracting parties to 65.
 “It has been an honor to steer ASEAN forward over the past year, alongside my fellow ASEAN leaders and partners, as we have navigated a very, very, very difficult year, and these are the crises that beset us,” Marcos said.
 Digital economy breakthrough 
 Marcos described the conclusion of negotiations on the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) as one of the major achievements of the Philippine chairship.
 He said the Philippines successfully steered the negotiations toward the agreement's conclusion and turnover within the year.
 “We are very proud of the DEFA because this is the first region-wide digital economy framework agreement in the whole world,” Marcos said.
 Once implemented, the agreement is expected to facilitate cross-border electronic commerce, establish common rules on data and digital payments, and help small businesses access markets beyond their home countries.
 Marcos stressed that ASEAN should actively participate in shaping the future of the digital economy.
 “We do not accept that ASEAN should just be customers to the AI revolution, but that we should be part of guiding the directions in which that development will take place, and that I think is the difference,” he said.
 Advancing energy security 
 On energy cooperation, Marcos cited progress in operationalizing the enhanced memorandum of understanding on the ASEAN Power Grid, which provides institutional planning and regulatory foundations for cross-border electricity connectivity.
 He also announced that preparations are underway for the first undersea power cable connecting Sabah, Malaysia, and Mindanao in the Philippines.
 The project marks an expansion of regional energy-sharing initiatives, which previously focused on land-based connections, he said.
 ASEAN also welcomed a regional framework aimed at strengthening disaster preparedness and response, particularly as climate change intensifies extreme weather events across Southeast Asia.
 Marcos said the initiative would improve coordination among member states in forecasting, rescue operations, humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.
 “This strengthens interoperability and this streamlines processes to improve our region's effective response to disasters. This is a recognition that the climate change is well and truly here,” he said.
 Marcos said the Summit's outcomes reflect the Philippines’ commitment to making regional cooperation more responsive to the needs of ASEAN member states. (PNA)
